name: record_live
description: Use when you need to see how engine values change over a few seconds: min / avg / max and whether each is rising, falling or steady.
instructions: Call record_live with up to 4 Mode 01 PIDs and 3-15 seconds, e.g. {"pids":["0105","010C"],"seconds":10}. It polls every 0.5 s.

Use it instead of read_live when the question is about change: a warm-up curve (coolant 0105), idle stability (rpm 010C), boost or MAP following rpm (010B with 010C), fuel trims drifting (0106 / 0107), module voltage while charging (0142).
Record related PIDs together in one call so their trends line up in time.
PIDs the car does not support come back as "Not supported on this car": do not ask for them again.
interpret: Each line is min / avg / max over the window plus a trend: the mean of the last third against the mean of the first third, steady when the change is under 1 or 5 % of the average.
Coolant rising steadily after a cold start is a normal warm-up; coolant falling while the engine idles warm points to a thermostat stuck open or a sensor fault.
A wide min-max spread with a steady trend means the value swings around a constant level (e.g. an unstable idle), not that it drifts.
Module voltage (0142) with the engine running under 13.5 V means the alternator is not charging; falling over the window means the battery is being drained.
A short recording shows a few seconds only: a trend here does not prove a long-term drift.
